Examine dependence across periods in firms' sales growth rates.
Select firms using beginning-of-period sales, firm age, and industry conditions for 2010–11, and calculate Spearman rank correlations over ten periods from 2010–11 through 2019–20.
Also use growth in 2010–11 and 2011–12 to calculate a tail dependence measure and cumulative means of growth in the following period after transforming it to nonnegative values.
Include zero growth in both analyses.

## 1 Rank correlations of growth rates

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(pins)
library(hrbrthemes)
library(kableExtra)
theme_set(theme_ipsum(base_size = 12, axis_title_size = 13))
board <- board_folder("../Zipf_law_board_replicate_simulation")
```

**Setting sample conditions**

Load `sample_growth_tb` and calculate firm age `age` as the beginning year extracted from period label `year` minus establishment year `birth_year`.
For 2010–11 growth records (`g_11_10`), save the `id` values of firms meeting the following conditions in `id_tb`.

* Beginning-of-period sales `pre_sale` of at least $4.0 \times 10^4$  
  With sales measured in thousands of yen, this corresponds to at least 40 million yen.
* Beginning-of-period firm age of at least five  
* The first two digits of industry code `ind_class` are 01–61 or 68–92

Use this set of firms for both rank correlations and tail analyses. Do not impose additional restrictions based on beginning-of-period sales, firm age, or industry in other periods.

Define `pobs()` to transform growth rates into rank-based pseudo-observations.
Use average ranks for ties and divide by the length of the original vector plus one.

<!-- Leave missing values in their original positions. -->

```{r}

library(corrr)
library(scattermore)

pobs <- function(x) {
  rank(x, ties.method = "average", na.last = "keep") / (length(x) + 1)
}

sample_growth_tb <- board |> pin_read("sample_growth_tb", type = "qs2") |> 
  mutate(age = as.numeric(str_c(20, str_sub(year, 6,7))) - birth_year) 

id_tb <- sample_growth_tb |> 
  filter(year == "g_11_10", 
         pre_sale >= 4.0*10^4, 
         age >= 5, 
         str_sub(ind_class, 1,2) %in% str_pad(c(1:61, 68:92), 2, pad = 0)) |> 
  distinct(id)

```

**Data for the two-period tail analysis**

Reshape growth rates for the selected firms to wide format and extract 2011–12 (`g_12_11`) and 2010–11 (`g_11_10`).
Retain only firms with finite growth rates in both periods in `normal_tb`.
Exclude `NA`, `NaN`, and positive or negative infinity, but retain zero.
Transform growth in each period to ranks separately using `pobs()`.
 
```{r}

normal_tb <- sample_growth_tb |> 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = id, names_from = "year", values_from = "growth") |> 
  inner_join(id_tb, by = "id") |> 
  select(g_12_11, g_11_10) |> 
  filter(is.finite(g_12_11), is.finite(g_11_10)) |>
  mutate(pobs_12_11 = pobs(g_12_11), pobs_11_10 = pobs(g_11_10)) 

```

**Spearman rank correlations across ten periods**

Reshape annual growth rates from 2010–11 through 2019–20 to wide format and calculate the Spearman rank correlation matrix for firms in `id_tb`.
Include zero growth.
At this stage, require a common sample with finite growth rates in all ten periods.

```{r}

spearman_mat_tb <- sample_growth_tb |> 
  filter(year %in% c("g_20_19", "g_19_18", "g_18_17", "g_17_16", "g_16_15", 
                     "g_15_14", "g_14_13", "g_13_12", "g_12_11", "g_11_10")) |> 
  select(id, year, growth) |> 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = id, names_from = "year", values_from = "growth") |> 
  inner_join(id_tb, by = "id") |> 
  select(-id) |> 
  filter(if_all(everything(), is.finite)) |>
  correlate(method = "spearman") 
spearman_mat_tb 

```

## 2 Dependence in the tail

**Tail dependence measure**

Let $N$ be the number of firms in `normal_tb` and $N_q$ the number whose pseudo-observations strictly exceed threshold $q$ in both periods.
Calculate the tail dependence measure as $N_q/[N(1-q)]$.
Vary $q$ from 0.8 to 0.9995 in increments of 0.0005 and save the measure at each threshold in `tail_tb`.

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2

tail_tb <- seq(0.8, 0.9995, by = 0.0005) |> 
  map_dfr(~ normal_tb |> 
            filter(pobs_12_11 > .x, pobs_11_10 > .x) |> 
            summarise(criteria = .x,
                      tail_coeff = (n()/nrow(normal_tb))/(1 - .x))
          )

tail_tb |> 
ggplot(aes(criteria, tail_coeff)) + 
  geom_line(size = 0.8, color = "steelblue") + 
  ylim(0, 0.3) + 
  labs(x = expression(q), 
       y = "Tail dependence") + 
  theme(axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"))  
ggsave(filename = "tail_coeff_TSR.png", path = "graph")

```

**Cumulative mean of nonnegative growth in the following period**

Sort `normal_tb` by descending growth in 2010–11, transform growth in the following period (2011–12) to $\max(g_{12,11}, 0)$, and calculate its cumulative mean.
Plot 2010–11 growth $t$ on the horizontal axis and the cumulative mean of nonnegative growth in the following period on the vertical axis to examine subsequent growth among firms that experienced large growth.
Calculate cumulative means using all of `normal_tb`, restricting only the displayed horizontal range to 0.2–2 and vertical range to 0–0.5.

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2

normal_tb |> 
  arrange(desc(g_11_10)) |> 
  mutate(
    g_12_11 = if_else(g_12_11 > 0, g_12_11, 0),
    cummean_12_11 = cummean(g_12_11)
  ) |> 
ggplot(aes(g_11_10, cummean_12_11)) +  
  geom_scattermore(pointsize = 1.5, color = "steelblue") + 
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.2, 2), ylim = c(0, 0.5)) + 
  labs(x = "t", 
       y = "Conditional tail expectation") + 
  theme(axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"))  
ggsave(filename = "cond_tail_expect_g_11_10_transformed.png", path = "graph")

```

## 3 LaTeX table output

Save the rank correlation matrix `spearman_mat_tb` to `latex/spearman_mat.tex` in the same folder as this QMD.
Leave correlation coefficients and row and column orders unchanged, formatting values to three decimal places only for output. Display missing values, including diagonal entries, as `--`.
Convert period labels in row and column headings, for example from `g_11_10` to `2010--11`.
Wrap period labels in `\mbox{}` to prevent line breaks and, as in `02_summ_stat.qmd`, use `tabularx` to fit the table to the text width. To reduce column spacing and display larger text, use a 9-point font and 0.5-point padding on each side of columns (`\tabcolsep`). Do not specify automatic resizing with `scale_down`.
Use the same rules and alternating row shading as the LaTeX tables in `02_summ_stat.qmd`, specifying the `table` environment and centering in the paper itself. Load the `tabularx` package in the paper. If text overflows because of the text width or font, adjust the font size further.

```{r}

# Leave the original correlation matrix unchanged and format a copy for output.
spearman_for_tex <- as.data.frame(spearman_mat_tb)
spearman_for_tex[[1]] <- str_replace(
  spearman_for_tex[[1]], "^g_(\\d{2})_(\\d{2})$", "20\\2--\\1"
)
period_labels <- str_replace(
  names(spearman_for_tex)[-1], "^g_(\\d{2})_(\\d{2})$", "20\\2--\\1"
)

# Prevent line breaks within period labels in row and column headings.
spearman_for_tex[[1]] <- paste0(
  "\\mbox{", spearman_for_tex[[1]], "}"
)
period_labels <- paste0("\\mbox{", period_labels, "}")

for (column in names(spearman_for_tex)[-1]) {
  spearman_for_tex[[column]] <- ifelse(
    is.na(spearman_for_tex[[column]]),
    "--",
    sprintf("%.3f", spearman_for_tex[[column]])
  )
}

spearman_tex <- spearman_for_tex |>
  kbl(
    format = "latex",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    row.names = FALSE,
    escape = FALSE,
    align = c("l", rep("r", length(period_labels))),
    col.names = c("Year", period_labels),
    linesep = ""
  ) |>
  kable_styling(
    latex_options = "striped",
    stripe_color = "gray!10",
    stripe_index = which(seq_len(nrow(spearman_for_tex)) %% 2L == 1L),
    full_width = TRUE,
    position = "left",
    font_size = 9
  )

writeLines(
  c(
    "\\begingroup",
    "\\setlength{\\tabcolsep}{0.5pt}",
    "\\renewcommand{\\arraystretch}{1.12}",
    "\\setlength{\\aboverulesep}{0.5ex}",
    "\\setlength{\\belowrulesep}{0.5ex}",
    "\\setlength{\\heavyrulewidth}{0.8pt}",
    "\\setlength{\\lightrulewidth}{0.4pt}",
    as.character(spearman_tex),
    "\\endgroup"
  ),
  con = file.path("latex", "spearman_mat.tex"),
  useBytes = TRUE
)
```
